questions.prompt: Why can't you score slot masks by comparing slot i with ground-truth object i?
options: Slots are an unordered set, so the pairing must be found by an assignment (e.g. Hungarian) before scoring.
Slots have a different dimensionality from objects, so their masks cannot be put in a common space.
Slot i always captures the background, so comparing it with object i would double count it.
Masks and slots live in different coordinate frames, so they cannot be compared pixel by pixel.
questions.explanation: Slot order is arbitrary; evaluation must be permutation invariant.

questions.prompt: Slot attention with identity projections, d=2, slots s1=(1,0), s2=(0,1), input x=(2,0). What attention weight does x give slot 1 after the softmax over slots? (3 decimals)
Two slots, inputs get slot-1 attention (0.9, 0.5, 0.1). After normalising over inputs, what weight does the first input have in slot 1's update? (3 decimals)
In slot attention, which normalisation makes slots compete for input features?
options: A softmax over the input axis for each slot.
A softmax over the slot axis for each input feature.
questions.explanation: Each input divides its attention among slots, so a slot gains only at the expense of others.

questions.prompt: A track predicts a detection with variance 0.04 per axis. A detection is 0.3 m off in x and 0.3 m in y. What is the squared Mahalanobis distance (isotropic)? (1 decimal)
A constant-velocity track was last seen at x=1.0 m with velocity 0.5 m/frame. It is occluded for 3 frames. What is its predicted x on the 4th frame after the last sighting (m, 1 decimal)?
Design a test of whether an object-centric representation keeps an object's identity when it is occluded. State the setup, metric, baseline and what outcome would reject the claim.
rubric: Setup with an object hidden for a controlled number of frames and known ground-truth identity.
Metric such as identity errors versus occlusion length, compared to a no-memory or position-only baseline.
A falsifier fixed in advance, e.g. errors not lower than the baseline beyond a given occlusion length.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
